working_memory.text: The Holloway town clock, which has stood over the market hall since 1911, has been stopped for the first time in decades while its pendulum is repaired. The clock lost about a minute a day after a bearing wore through, and the clockmaker found the pendulum rod had also bent slightly. Both parts will be made new to the original drawings, which the town still holds. The chimes will be silent for about six weeks. The clock's four faces are being cleaned while the mechanism is out.
